You want iaso to approve a record by itself only when it is sure, and to ask you otherwise. Nothing you said rules out searching your past sessions for a record's words.

The code has changed how it asks about an older record (one whose words iaso never logged). Before, the judge had to supply the quote, or the question waited. Now the quote is optional. If the judge gives no quote, iaso looks for the record's own words in your past session transcripts and quotes them with the day it found them. That still matches example 1.

When nothing is found, iaso now adds one fixed line: "I found none of your words about this in your past sessions." It then relies on the judge's own question wording. Nothing in the code still makes sure the question asks what you meant, which example 2 requires.

The change also does two other things:
- It drops a question you seem to have answered already.
- It searches the transcripts even for records whose words were logged, as a fallback.

The code points to two of your decisions (DEC-191 and DEC-192) that make the quote optional, so the change looks deliberate. But the turn behind it has no text, so I can't tell whether you meant the "not found" question to stop always asking what you meant.
